## Problem 1

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(gfoRmula)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read in the data
data <- read_csv("hw7data_HIV_2024.csv")

# Define treatment combinations
treatment_combinations <- list(
  a_0000 = c(0, 0, 0, 0),
  a_0001 = c(0, 0, 0, 1),
  a_0011 = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
  a_0111 = c(0, 1, 1, 1),
  a_1111 = c(1, 1, 1, 1)
)

# Define covariate models explicitly
cov_models <- list(
  A0 = glm(A0 ~ R0 + CD40, family = binomial(), data = data),
  R1 = glm(R1 ~ R0 + CD40 + A0, family = binomial(), data = data),
  CD41 = glm(CD41 ~ CD40 + A0 + R1, family = gaussian(), data = data),
  A1 = glm(A1 ~ R1 + CD41 + A0, family = binomial(), data = data),
  R2 = glm(R2 ~ R1 + CD41 + A1, family = binomial(), data = data),
  CD42 = glm(CD42 ~ CD41 + A1 + R2, family = gaussian(), data = data),
  A2 = glm(A2 ~ R2 + CD42 + A1, family = binomial(), data = data),
  R3 = glm(R3 ~ R2 + CD42 + A2, family = binomial(), data = data),
  CD43 = glm(CD43 ~ CD42 + A2 + R3, family = gaussian(), data = data),
  A3 = glm(A3 ~ R3 + CD43 + A2, family = binomial(), data = data),
  R4 = glm(R4 ~ R3 + CD43 + A3, family = binomial(), data = data)
)

# Fit the outcome model
outcome_model <- glm(CD44 ~ CD43 + A3 + R4, family = gaussian(), data = data)

# Define a function to simulate each treatment combination
simulate_treatment <- function(treatment_comb) {
  # Create a copy of the dataset for simulation
  sim_data <- data
  
  # Simulate each time step
  sim_data$A0 <- treatment_comb[1]
  sim_data$R1 <- predict(cov_models$R1, newdata = sim_data, type = "response")
  sim_data$R1 <- ifelse(runif(nrow(sim_data)) < sim_data$R1, 1, 0)  # Convert probabilities to binary
  
  sim_data$CD41 <- predict(cov_models$CD41, newdata = sim_data)
  
  sim_data$A1 <- treatment_comb[2]
  sim_data$R2 <- predict(cov_models$R2, newdata = sim_data, type = "response")
  sim_data$R2 <- ifelse(runif(nrow(sim_data)) < sim_data$R2, 1, 0)
  
  sim_data$CD42 <- predict(cov_models$CD42, newdata = sim_data)
  
  sim_data$A2 <- treatment_comb[3]
  sim_data$R3 <- predict(cov_models$R3, newdata = sim_data, type = "response")
  sim_data$R3 <- ifelse(runif(nrow(sim_data)) < sim_data$R3, 1, 0)
  
  sim_data$CD43 <- predict(cov_models$CD43, newdata = sim_data)
  
  sim_data$A3 <- treatment_comb[4]
  sim_data$R4 <- predict(cov_models$R4, newdata = sim_data, type = "response")
  sim_data$R4 <- ifelse(runif(nrow(sim_data)) < sim_data$R4, 1, 0)
  
  # Predict the outcome (CD44) based on the simulated data
  predicted_outcomes <- predict(outcome_model, newdata = sim_data)
  
  # Return the mean predicted outcome and standard error
  list(
    mean = mean(predicted_outcomes),
    se = sd(predicted_outcomes) / sqrt(nrow(sim_data))
  )
}


# Simulate and collect results for each treatment combination
results <- lapply(treatment_combinations, simulate_treatment)

# Format and display results
results_summary <- data.frame(
  Treatment = names(treatment_combinations),
  Estimate = sapply(results, `[[`, "mean"),
  SE = sapply(results, `[[`, "se")
)

cat("Estimated Anticipated Response and Standard Errors:\n")
print(results_summary)

```

## Problem 2

### Part a

The following logistic regression model gets propensity scores for each year for each patient. The year_round variable is included in the model along with the other covariates because the patients are more likely to have had the transplant as they get later into the study period.

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read in the data
data <- read_csv("hw7data_liver_2024.csv")

# Fit the logistic regression model to estimate propensity scores for transplantation
propensity_model <- glm(
  transplanted ~ year_round + age + sex + edema + serBilir + albumin + prothrombin,
  family = binomial(),
  data = data
)

# Add propensity scores to the dataset
data <- data %>%
  mutate(pscore = predict(propensity_model, type = "response"))

summary(propensity_model)

```

### Part b

```{r}
# Step 1: Add a unique ID for each patient if not already present
data <- data %>% mutate(id = as.character(id))

# Step 2: Calculate propensity scores for each year
# Pivot the data to create columns for propensity scores by year
pscores_by_year <- data %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarize(
    pscore_0 = first(pscore[year_round == 0], default = NA),
    pscore_1 = first(pscore[year_round == 1], default = NA),
    pscore_2 = first(pscore[year_round == 2], default = NA),
    pscore_3 = first(pscore[year_round == 3], default = NA),
    pscore_4 = first(pscore[year_round == 4], default = NA),
    pscore_5 = first(pscore[year_round == 5], default = NA),
    pscore_6 = first(pscore[year_round == 6], default = NA),
    died_anytime = as.integer(any(dead == 1))  # Indicator for death at any point
  )

# Step 3: Add compliance columns for each treatment rule
treatment_rules <- list(
  rule_0 = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  rule_1 = c(0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  rule_2 = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  rule_3 = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1),
  rule_4 = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1),
  rule_5 = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1),
  rule_6 = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1),
  rule_never = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
)


# Initialize the compliance dataframe
data_compliance <- data.frame(id = unique(data$id))

# Function to evaluate compliance with a single rule
evaluate_compliance <- function(transplanted_sequence, rule_sequence) {
  # Truncate the treatment rule to the length of the patient's sequence
  truncated_rule <- rule_sequence[seq_along(transplanted_sequence)]
  # Check if the truncated rule matches the transplanted sequence
  all(transplanted_sequence == truncated_rule)
}

# Loop through each patient and calculate compliance for each rule
for (patient_id in unique(data$id)) {
  # Extract the transplanted sequence for this patient
  patient_data <- data[data$id == patient_id, ]
  transplanted_sequence <- patient_data$transplanted
  
  # Initialize a vector to store compliance results
  compliance_results <- vector("logical", length(treatment_rules))
  
  # Loop through each treatment rule
  for (i in seq_along(treatment_rules)) {
    rule_name <- names(treatment_rules)[i]
    rule_sequence <- treatment_rules[[rule_name]]
    compliance_results[i] <- evaluate_compliance(transplanted_sequence, rule_sequence)
  }
  
  # Add compliance results to the dataframe
  data_compliance[data_compliance$id == patient_id, names(treatment_rules)] <- compliance_results
}


# Step 4: Combine propensity scores and compliance data into a single data frame
aggregated_data <- left_join(pscores_by_year, data_compliance, by = "id")

```

```{r}
# Add a column to indicate whether a patient died at any time during the study
aggregated_data <- aggregated_data %>%
  mutate(
    died = ifelse(id %in% (data %>% filter(dead == 1) %>% pull(id)), 1, 0)
  )

# Correctly calculate the weight denominator and add columns for each treatment rule
for (rule_name in names(treatment_rules)) {
  treatment_sequence <- treatment_rules[[rule_name]]  # Extract the treatment sequence for the rule
  
  aggregated_data <- aggregated_data %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      # Weight denominator: Correct product of propensity scores and (1 - propensity score)
      !!paste0("weight_denominator_", rule_name) := prod(
        ifelse(
          treatment_sequence == 1,
          c_across(starts_with("pscore")),        # Use pscore when treatment rule is 1
          1 - c_across(starts_with("pscore"))    # Use (1 - pscore) when treatment rule is 0
        ),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      
      # Weight numerator: Compliance indicator for the rule
      !!paste0("weight_numerator_", rule_name) := ifelse(get(rule_name), 1, 0),
      
      # IPW Weight: Numerator divided by denominator
      !!paste0("ipw_weight_", rule_name) := get(paste0("weight_numerator_", rule_name)) /
        get(paste0("weight_denominator_", rule_name))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Initialize a data frame to store the results
ipw_results <- data.frame(
  Rule = names(treatment_rules),
  Estimate = numeric(length(treatment_rules))
)

# Loop through each treatment rule and calculate the IPW estimate
for (rule_name in names(treatment_rules)) {
  # Use the corresponding weight column
  ipw_estimate <- sum(aggregated_data$died * aggregated_data[[paste0("ipw_weight_", rule_name)]], na.rm = TRUE) /
    sum(aggregated_data[[paste0("ipw_weight_", rule_name)]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Store the estimate in the results data frame
  ipw_results[ipw_results$Rule == rule_name, "Estimate"] <- ipw_estimate
}

# Print the IPW results
cat("IPW Estimates for Mean Response by Treatment Rule:\n")
print(ipw_results)

```




```{r,results='hide'}
# Initialize a variable to store the weighted sum
weighted_sum <- 0
total_compliance_count <- 0

# Loop through each treatment rule
for (rule_name in names(treatment_rules)) {
  # Get the sum of compliance for the rule
  rule_compliance_count <- sum(aggregated_data[[rule_name]], na.rm = TRUE)
  print(rule_compliance_count)
  
  # Get the IPW estimate for the rule
  ipw_estimate <- ipw_results$Estimate[ipw_results$Rule == rule_name]
  
  # Add the weighted contribution to the total
  weighted_sum <- weighted_sum + (rule_compliance_count * ipw_estimate)
  total_compliance_count <- total_compliance_count + rule_compliance_count
}

# Calculate the overall mean by dividing by the total number of patients
overall_mean_from_rules <- weighted_sum / total_compliance_count

# Calculate the actual overall mean
actual_overall_mean <- mean(aggregated_data$died, na.rm = TRUE)

# Print the results
cat("Validation Check:\n")
cat("Overall Mean from Rules:", overall_mean_from_rules, "\n")
cat("Actual Overall Mean:", actual_overall_mean, "\n")

if (abs(overall_mean_from_rules - actual_overall_mean) < 1e-6) {
  cat("The IPW calculations are consistent with the overall mean.\n")
} else {
  cat("There is a discrepancy in the IPW calculations. Please review the code.\n")
}

```

### Part c

```{r}
set.seed(123) # For reproducibility

# Number of bootstrap samples
num_bootstrap <- 1000

# Initialize a matrix to store bootstrap estimates
bootstrap_estimates <- matrix(NA, nrow = num_bootstrap, ncol = length(treatment_rules))
colnames(bootstrap_estimates) <- names(treatment_rules)

# Bootstrap procedure
for (b in 1:num_bootstrap) {
  # Resample the data with replacement
  bootstrap_data <- aggregated_data[sample(nrow(aggregated_data), replace = TRUE), ]
  
  # Recalculate IPW estimates for each treatment rule
  for (rule_name in names(treatment_rules)) {
    # Recalculate weights
    bootstrap_data <- bootstrap_data %>%
      mutate(!!paste0("weight_numerator_", rule_name) := ifelse(get(rule_name), 1, 0),
             !!paste0("ipw_weight_", rule_name) := get(paste0("weight_numerator_", rule_name)) /
                                                   get(paste0("weight_denominator_", rule_name)))
    
    # Calculate the IPW estimate
    ipw_estimate <- sum(bootstrap_data$died * bootstrap_data[[paste0("ipw_weight_", rule_name)]], na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(bootstrap_data[[paste0("ipw_weight_", rule_name)]], na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Store the estimate in the bootstrap matrix
    bootstrap_estimates[b, rule_name] <- ipw_estimate
  }
}

# Calculate standard errors from bootstrap estimates
bootstrap_se <- apply(bootstrap_estimates, 2, sd)

# Add standard errors to the IPW results
ipw_results$Standard_Error <- bootstrap_se

# Print the results
cat("IPW Estimates with Standard Errors from Bootstrap:\n")
print(ipw_results)

# Optional: Save bootstrap results for further analysis
write.csv(ipw_results, "ipw_results_with_bootstrap_se.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```
